name: SLABBERJAN
description: Slabberjan is a traditional Dutch elimination game, specific to Zeeland, where players swap 'pieces' (originally cards, now custom tiles/tokens called 'Doppen') to avoid holding the lowest rank at the end of a round. It is remarkably similar to the card game 'Gnav' or 'Cuckoo'. The game involves bluffing, special 'Matador' pieces that block swaps (Knight, Bird, Cat, Inn), and a pot that the loser must pay into. The last player with chips wins.

content.text: Slabberjan is a traditional Dutch elimination game, specific to Zeeland, where players swap 'pieces' (originally cards, now custom tiles/tokens called 'Doppen') to avoid holding the lowest rank at the end of a round. It is remarkably similar to the card game 'Gnav' or 'Cuckoo'. The game involves bluffing, special 'Matador' pieces that block swaps (Knight, Bird, Cat, Inn), and a pot that the loser must pay into. The last player with chips wins.
Derived from the 18th-century card games 'Gnav' (Danish) and 'Vogelspiel' (German). When cards were banned/taxed, players switched to wooden pieces.

From two up to twenty or more in the parent game Gnav; the Zeeland variant Slabberjan is typically played with five to fifteen players for the best experience. Since each player receives one piece from the set of 42, two to forty-two players are possible.
42 pieces. Ranking: Knight (Kap-af) > Bird > Cat > Inn > 12 > 11... > 0 > White Bread > Pot > Face > Fool (Jan Rit).

Each player draws 1 piece from a bag. Kept secret.

items.text: Gnav (Norwegian/Danish): Original Norwegian and Danish game with slightly different piece names and order: Cuckoo (stops trading), Knight (cut off), Cat (undo swaps), Horse, House (pass to next). Played with 42 cards or pawns; 2 to 20 or more players.
Slabberjan (Zeeland): Zeeland variant with Ruiter/Kap-af (knight), Vogel (bird), Poesje (cat), Herberg (inn); no horse; White Bread below zero. Played with 42 pieces only.
